title: Fifteen years of kept notes
subtitle: Why every sailing since 2011 is written down - and what the record does for yours.

sub: Sailings, ship visits and port days since 2011, written down at the time - not remembered fondly later.

items.head: Ships, walked
items.body: Which decks carry noise, which cabins sit beneath the pool deck, which suites earn their fare.

items.head: Ports, timed
items.body: How long the tender really takes, when the crowds land, when the light is worth the detour.

items.head: Fares, tracked
items.body: What a sailing was published at, what it quietly dropped to, and when in the year that happens.

title: You don't read the notebook. You get its verdict.
caption: Fifteen years condensed to a shortlist of three, with a reason attached to each.
brief: Jordan's engraved portrait stamp, centred on white - composed 4:5 from public/portrait-engraved.png.

points.label: The ship
points.value: Chosen against its sisters and its refit date, not its brochure.

points.label: The cabin
points.value: Picked off the deck plan, not the category name.

points.label: The season
points.value: Booked for light and crowds, not the headline fare.

points.label: The fare
points.value: Negotiated against what it actually sells for, not what it lists at.

text: Experience isn't the years. It's what you kept from them.
sub: Plenty of people have sailed for fifteen years. The difference is a written record - and one person reading it on your behalf.

title: Name a sailing you're weighing up
body: Send it in a DM - ship and month is enough. If the notebook has an opinion, you'll get its two-line verdict, candid and free of charge.
